The constant-size inner loops and missing-color sentinel are easy to explain, with no unnecessary abstraction or prohibited local name.

After the forward sweep reaches position i, `last` holds the greatest occurrence at or before i for every color, so the table contains the closest left-side distance. The reverse sweep analogously considers the least occurrence at or after i and keeps the smaller directional distance. Every possible occurrence lies on one of those sides, an exact match produces zero, and a globally absent color retains a distance at least n and becomes `-1`; direct table lookup therefore answers every query correctly.
